paragraphs: It is argued that applying advertisement in business can bring about advantages on economy, however some others say that this has bad impacts on emotional issues of people in their life. There are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

Admittedly, people who agree on support for advertisement say that the growth of advertising brings clear undeniable economic benefits. This means that commercials have many creative contents which appeal visual effects. Addition to, so customers can be attracted by interesting and powerful advertisements, playing a role in meeting demands of them and subsequently make informed purchasing decisions in a far wide scale. This plays a advertising creates jobs in marketing, media and design which makes an important driver of economic activity.

However, others who think that advertising has negative social consequences. This is primarily because advertisements constantly show images of perfect lifestyles, beauty standards, or luxury possessions. This tendency would foster dissatisfaction among viewers. It can be seen clearly in young people who feel pressured to buy trendy clothes or the latest smart gadgets advertised on TikTok or Facebook. This undoubtedly leads to frustration when they cannot afford them. Furthermore, in the long run commercials would promote materialistic values and a money-driven culture.
Overall, I strongly believe that both views valid to come certain extent. Advertising contributes to dissatisfaction but even provides notable benefits in the economy or the growth of the economy.

paragraphs: Commercial advertising can bring advantages to businesses and the wider economy, whereas some people argue that it creates harmful emotional pressure in everyday life. Advertising can inform consumers about products and support trade, although its idealised images can also affect how people evaluate themselves and their possessions. There are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

On the one hand, supporters of advertising often point to the undeniable economic benefits it can bring. Creative content and appealing visual effects can attract customers and stimulate consumer demand. Increased demand encourages people to make purchases, allowing firms to expand production on a wider scale. This expansion can create employment opportunities and generate greater state revenue through taxation. Digital retailers can use powerful advertising campaigns to reach more customers. Furthermore, the advertising industry creates direct jobs in marketing, media and design, which makes it an important driver of economic activity.

Those on the other side of the debate, however, argue that advertising entails negative social consequences. Advertisements constantly show images of perfect lifestyles, beauty standards and luxury possessions, which may foster dissatisfaction among viewers. Young people may feel pressured to buy trendy clothes or the latest smart gadgets advertised on TikTok or Facebook. This pressure can lead to frustration when those items are beyond their budget. Furthermore, repeated commercial messages may promote materialistic values and a money-driven culture in the long run, as people can start to associate personal worth with expensive possessions.

In conclusion, both views are valid to a certain extent. Advertising can support economic development through consumer demand, production and employment. At the same time, it can contribute to social dissatisfaction and materialistic values.

paragraphs: Nowadays, the news media are appearing more frequently in our daily lives. Despite the irrefutable benefits, this news entail largely inevitable drawbacks. Personally, I am of first school of thought.

I firmly believe that, the news media have a big influence on people's lives. This is because that with the presence of the widespread success to smartphones and the internet, these technologies allow people to follow the news instantly. Additionally, news become a regular part of people's routine. Moreover, the intense competition among new outlets appears popularly with the purpose of gain attention. Today, most idea agencies focus on shocking and breaking content. This means that those news are presented in a highly sensationalized manner with dramatic headlines and eye-catching visuals. It naturally follows that this reinforces the overall impact of news on public opinion.

However, I strongly believe that the bad influence of news is true but it also brings undeniable benefits. With exposure to a constant stream of distressing and exaggerated news, people are easily overwhelmed. This, without any doubt - people feel overly anxious and helpless even in situations that do not directly affect them. By contrast, news coverage serves a virtual function as it constantly warns people to existing and looming problems in society - such as crime, natural disasters, or political corruption. To addition, individuals would have be better informed and more prepared to respond to potential threats, which plays a role in handling risks more carefully in an increasingly complex society.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that although the adding more news media offers certain advantages, it leads to drawbacks inevitably.

paragraphs: Nowadays, the news media are appearing more frequently in our daily lives. Despite the irrefutable benefits, this news can entail significant drawbacks. Personally, I acknowledge the strong influence of news media, although I do not consider its effects entirely negative.

I firmly believe that the news media have a big influence on people's lives. This is because widespread access to smartphones and the Internet allows people to use these technologies to follow the news instantly, wherever and whenever they are. As a result, news becomes a regular part of people's routine. Moreover, the intense competition among news outlets is widespread as these outlets seek to gain attention. Today, most media agencies focus on shocking and breaking content. This means that this news is presented in a highly sensationalized manner with dramatic headlines and eye-catching visuals. It naturally follows that this reinforces the overall impact of news on public opinion.

However, I strongly believe that the bad influence of news is real, yet news also brings undeniable benefits. With exposure to a constant stream of distressing and exaggerated news, people are easily overwhelmed. This, without any doubt, makes people feel overly anxious and helpless even in situations that do not directly affect them. By contrast, news coverage serves a vital function as it constantly warns people to existing and looming problems in society - such as crime, natural disasters, or political corruption. As a result, individuals would be better informed and more prepared to respond to potential threats, which plays a role in handling risks more carefully in an increasingly complex society.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that the news media have a strong influence on people's lives: although this influence offers certain advantages, it can also lead to drawbacks.

paragraphs: It is argued that educational organization should reward students who have the best academic performances, while others say that rewarding students who show improvements is more essential. Personally, I believe that recognizing both groups of students is completely suitable.

Admittedly, since students who have the best academic results are received rewards, they have diligently applied themselves to their studies. This is because they deserve their praises and privileges which may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, leading to propel towards overall academic gains. Moreover, this kind of competition can be easily seen in almost every aspect of life where only the best individuals are rewarded. It naturally follows that students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition which play an important role in enabling students to achieve success in later life.

However, I strongly believe that recognizing students who show notable improvements is wise in the way of educating. When only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards others would think that their effort is futile because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals. Accordingly, those students prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened. As a results, they gradually lose the incentive to study. Furthermore, emphasizing improvements also encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help them to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves. This makes students realize irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. Consequently, the constant desire to outdo themselves, which even benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that both groups of students should be received rewards from their schools because of undeniable benefits.

paragraphs: It is argued that educational organizations should reward students who have the best academic results, while others say that rewarding students who show improvements is more essential. Personally, I believe that recognizing both groups of students is appropriate.

Admittedly, students with the best academic results should be rewarded. First, these students have diligently applied themselves to their studies, and they deserve their praises and privileges which may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards, thereby contributing to overall academic gains. Moreover, this kind of competition can be easily seen in almost every aspect of life where only the best individuals are rewarded. It naturally follows that students are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition which can play an important role in enabling students to achieve success in later life.

However, I strongly believe that recognizing students who show notable improvements is a sound educational approach. Initially, when only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, others would think that their effort is futile. This is because they may feel unable to surpass those outstanding individuals. Accordingly, these students are prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened. As a result, they gradually lose the incentive to study. Furthermore, emphasizing improvements also encourages all students to be diligent in their studies and helps them understand that they need to keep improving, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. Consequently, a constant desire to outdo themselves may benefit them more than the determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that both groups of students should receive rewards from their schools for the reasons discussed above.

review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: Nowadays in some countries, parents make a decision to educate their children at home instead of sending them to education organizations. Although such development is detrimental to a certain extent, I believe that the disadvantages that it offers are far more pronounced.

Admittedly, one might argue that children would develop better when they study at home. This is because homeschooling allow parents to save money that no school fees are required. Moreover, parents believe that home-educated children less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure which causes emotional and mental problems. In addition, when parents teach their children at home by themselves, they can tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young ones. This can not be seen in the case of traditional schooling because of the large class size.

However, this line of reasoning, I strongly believe, is not sound. This educational approach do not actually save money. This means that parents need to pay a large amount of money for lab equipment and tutors. Besides, one parent needs to be cut off and cater for their child's needs, be these academic or personal. Furthermore, most parents are not well versed in all school subjects. They might meet difficulties in properly explaining concepts for children and ultimately academic problems. In addition, even social problems that children can be faced with at school like bullying and having romantic feelings for others would prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.

In conclusion, although it is true that parents educate their children by themselves at home may bring about a few advantages, these are relatively minor and should not overshadow the far more significant and long-lasting benefits schools entail.
review.overall: Em có đủ bốn đoạn và kết bài chọn tác hại học tại nhà lớn hơn; cả sáu nhánh được nhắc. Tuy vậy, mở bài gọi cách học này 'detrimental to a certain extent' rồi nói bất lợi còn lớn hơn, làm câu nhượng bộ sai hướng. Body 1 dùng 'Admittedly' hợp vai trò nhưng vào lý do đầu bằng 'This is because' thay vì báo đây là nhánh thứ nhất; Body 2 nói 'this line of reasoning ... is not sound' rồi có các nhánh phản bác. Nhiều câu còn thiếu động từ chia hoặc dùng từ lệch: 'homeschooling allow', 'approach do not', 'meet difficulties'. Em cần sửa các câu này mà giữ lập trường nhất quán.

paragraphs: Nowadays, in some countries, parents decide to educate their children at home instead of sending them to schools. Although this approach is beneficial to a certain extent, I believe that its disadvantages are far more pronounced.

Admittedly, one might argue that homeschooling benefits both parents and children. Initially, homeschooling allows parents to save money as no school fees are required. Moreover, home-educated children are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, which can cause emotional and mental problems. In addition, when parents teach their children at home themselves, they can tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young ones. This is often not the case in traditional schooling owing to the large class size.

However, I strongly believe that these apparent benefits come with greater costs and developmental drawbacks. Initially, this approach may not actually save money: parents need to pay for lab equipment and tutors, and one parent may need to set aside working time to cater for the child's academic or personal needs. Furthermore, most parents are not well versed in all school subjects; therefore, they may have difficulty explaining concepts properly, which can lead to academic problems. In addition, even social problems that children face at school, such as bullying and having romantic feelings for others, can prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.

In conclusion, although educating children at home may bring a few advantages, its disadvantages outweigh those advantages, and the far more significant and long-lasting benefits schools entail make traditional schooling preferable.
